strengths: requireEmailVerified is a single pure middleware (server/src/middleware/email-gate.ts:3-17) matching the spec implementation exactly — server-enforced 403 JSON, not a redirect

Correct ordering in routes.ts: api.use(requireAuth) then the gate, so req.user.emailVerified is populated by requireAuth before the gate reads it; all board routers are mounted on `api` after the gate so none can bypass it
Gate is wrapped in its own dedicated flag `if (config.EMAIL_GATE_ENABLED === "true")` (routes.ts:41-43), independent of OAUTH_ENABLED, per spec Rollback Plan
req.user undefined falls through to next() (email-gate.ts:8-11), correctly leaving 401 handling to requireAuth — the [must-not] unauthenticated-403 case is satisfied
set-username/set-password bypass the gate: mounted on the separate /api/auth oauthRouter (index.ts:93), not on the `api` Router
No email_verified backfill introduced — the gate, not a data mutation, is the control (spec Scope + Rule 3)
Tests written and all 3 pass; they assert the exact `{ needsEmailVerification: true }` body, covering false/true/undefined branches

issues.description: Observation (not a T3 violation): the SHA range bundles T4 changes — index.ts (oauthRouter mount), routes/oauth.ts, and routes/oauth.test.ts are out of T3 scope. config.ts adds EMAIL_GATE_ENABLED, a legitimate T3 dependency (QUALITY BAR requires reading config.EMAIL_GATE_ENABLED; key was absent at T2 tip). The three strictly in-scope T3 files contain no out-of-scope edits.

Observation on bypass scope: gate applied only to the `api` Router. The sibling createAgentRouter() is also mounted at /api (index.ts:96) and is NOT behind the gate. Outside T3's DELIVERABLE (which scopes /api/workspaces board routes) and does not affect this verdict, but noted because the verification target is 'cannot be bypassed' — agent routes are a separate surface not covered by this middleware.
